question: Unfair competition from voluntary associations in tenders has, over time, become a sensitive and complex issue.

When they take part in tenders for patient transport in the Campania region of Italy, associations of that kind tender at the lowest possible rates, which they are able to do by replacing paid employees with volunteers, thus cutting labour costs to the extent that no economic operator of any other legal status can compete and win public contracts.

Voluntary associations are non-profit entities which, as a general rule, are active in social, cultural or humanitarian areas, but may still take part in calls for tender for public contracts, particularly in the area of social and health services. However, their inclusion in tenders can cause competition issues with companies that are run for profit.

In the light of the above, will the Commission ensure that the substitution of paid employees in the awarding of public contracts does not lead to the desertion of waged workers, rises in unemployment rates and the elimination of firms from the competitive public administration market?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (22.4.2025) As a general principle, public procurement procedures are open to all legal or natural persons willing to provide services, works or supplies. All bidders must be treated equally, regardless of their characteristics, including legal form, statutory goals, way of functioning or financing, and the use of voluntary staff.

Furthermore, EU public procurement rules allow public buyers to limit participation in a tender procedure to non-profit organisations only (CPV 85143000-3 Ambulance services)1. In the cases referred to, the public buyers involved did not decide to use this possibility.
1 Article 77 of Directive 2014/24 on public procurement.
